terra.problem: Saying nobody is packing a bag adds a detail the passage does not give.
The comparison about an oldest kid getting the first turn invokes a modern family scenario, which is outside the adult audience rules.
Jacob speaks about entering their council and joining their assembly. Saying he says it twice treats the two statements as identical.
Saying Jacob says it twice treats his statements about the council and the assembly as identical.
The passage does not say Simeon and Levi walked in together or that they will be spread apart from each other.
Judah's brothers lining up to cheer is an invented detail. Jacob says they will praise and bow down to him.
The hat joke does not follow a clear logic: bringing a tall hat because he is nervous has no clear connection to avoiding the lion.
The passage says the nations' allegiance is his, not that the nations belong with him. Capitalizing 'Him' also presents an identification the passage does not make.
The scepter not departing from Judah does not establish that nobody pries it from his hands. That adds a physical action to the image.
The passage does not say the vine is overflowing.
The passage does not say the vine is overflowing.
The text does not say Issachar stays put or does not go anywhere.
A day's work adds a duration the passage does not give and turns the donkey comparison into a literal action.
The passage does not describe the snake as small or say the rider is surprised.
The text says the rider tumbles backward, not that he looks at the sky.
Joseph steadying his bow does not establish that he stays in one place.
The text says Joseph's strong arms were tempered by God's hands. It does not say his strength did not come from his own muscles.
The passage does not say the wolf has its feet on the ground or works continuously from morning until evening.
Jacob compares Judah to a lion; he does not say Judah got a lion. He says Zebulun will become a harbor, not that he got one.
Saying Jacob is thinking about home assigns him a thought the passage does not state.
The statement that Jacob is lying in Egypt uses a fact from outside this passage without a reference.
